bottom_line: Empagliflozin vs placebo reduced the risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.86).
implications: These data support that, over a median of 16 months, empagliflozin compared with placebo lowered the risk of the primary composite outcome (hazard ratio 0.75; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.86) and lowered total heart-failure hospitalizations (hazard ratio 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85), while slowing eGFR decline (–0.55 vs. –2.28 ml/min/1.73 m2 per year, P<0.001). The result does not establish a reduction in cardiovascular death alone (0.92; 95% CI, 0.75 to 1.12) or death from any cause (0.92; 95% CI, 0.77 to 1.10), and uncomplicated genital tract infection was more frequent with empagliflozin.

major_points.text: Double-blind randomized trial in chronic heart failure (NYHA II–IV) with LVEF ≤40%, empagliflozin 10 mg daily vs placebo on top of recommended therapy.
major_points.quote: In this double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 3730 patients with class II, III, or IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less to receive empagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or placebo, in addition to recommended therapy.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was a composite of adjudicated cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure (time to first event).
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a compos- ite of adjudicated cardiovascular death or hospi- talization for heart failure, analyzed as the time to the first event.

major_points.text: Primary outcome occurred less often with empagliflozin than placebo (HR 0.75; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001).
major_points.quote: a primary outcome event occurred in 361 of 1863 patients (19.4%) in the empagliflozin group and in 462 of 1867 patients (24.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio for cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Total (first and recurrent) hospitalizations for heart failure were lower with empagliflozin (hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85; P<0.001).
major_points.quote: The total number of hospitalizations for heart failure was lower in the empagliflozin group than in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85; P<0.001).

major_points.text: The annual rate of decline in eGFR was slower with empagliflozin than placebo (–0.55 vs. –2.28 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area per year, P<0.001).
major_points.quote: The annual rate of decline in the esti- mated glomerular filtration rate was slower in the empagliflozin group than in the placebo group (–0.55 vs. –2.28 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area per year, P<0.001)

major_points.text: Uncomplicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently with empagliflozin.
major_points.quote: Uncomplicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently with empagliflozin.

inclusion_criteria.text: Adults (≥18 years of age) with chronic heart failure (NYHA class II, III, or IV) and LVEF ≤40%.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Adults (≥18 years of age) who had chronic heart failure (functional class II, III, or IV) with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% or less were eligible to participate in the trial.

criticisms.text: Some patients had unknown vital status at trial end and some were lost to follow-up, partly due to Covid-19 operational challenges.
criticisms.quote: A total of 21 patients (0.6%) had unknown vital status at the end of the trial, in part related to operational challenges associ- ated with coronavirus disease 2019 (Covid-19);

criticisms.text: Some patients were lost to follow-up before the data cutoff.
criticisms.quote: 42 patients (20 in the placebo group and 22 in the empagliflozin group), including those with unknown vital status, were lost to follow-up at various times before the data cutoff.
